study_notes.topic: Classification or Odd One Out (Verbal Reasoning)

sections.title: Advanced Strategy for Level 3 Classification
sections.content: At Level 3, the pattern is hidden and multi-layered. Step 1: Break each option into smaller parts. Step 2: Look for possible mathematical, linguistic, or factual relationships. Step 3: Confirm the rule through multiple steps. Step 4: Apply the same rule to all options. Step 5: The option that does not follow the rule will be the Odd One Out.

sections.title: 3-Tier Number Logic
sections.content: Step 1: Break the 4-digit number into individual digits. Step 2: Multiply the first and last digits. Step 3: Multiply the second and third digits. Step 4: Add the two results. Step 5: Check whether the sum is a prime number. Example: 2134 → (2 × 4) + (1 × 3) = 8 + 3 = 11 (prime). If any number does not produce a prime sum, that will be the Odd One Out.

sections.title: Deep Factual Word Logic
sections.content: Step 1: Identify the meaning or category of all words. Step 2: Check whether they belong to a specific group or subcategory. Step 3: Confirm the relationship using factual knowledge. Step 4: Select the word that does not belong to that specific category as the Odd One Out. Example: Habeas Corpus, Mandamus, Certiorari, Impeachment. The first three are constitutional writs in India, while Impeachment is a different constitutional process.

sections.title: Alphanumeric Hybrid Classification
sections.content: Step 1: Convert letters into their alphabetical positions (A=1, B=2 ... Z=26). Step 2: Find the difference or sum between the two letters. Step 3: Apply a mathematical operation on that difference (such as square or cube). Step 4: Match the result with the middle number. Step 5: The option that does not follow this pattern will be the Odd One Out. Example: A9D → A=1, D=4 → difference = 3 → 3² = 9.

sections.title: Common Mistakes
sections.content: 1. Jumping to conclusions in complex number patterns. 2. Not knowing the correct factual meaning of words. 3. Using incorrect alphabetical values. 4. Not verifying the complete multi-step logic.

sections.title: Quick Summary
sections.content: Level 3 classification involves multi-layer logic. In numbers, apply multi-step mathematical relationships; in words, identify deeper factual categories; and in alphanumeric problems, recognize combined patterns of letters and numbers.

tricks.title: Prime Check Shortcut
tricks.explanation: If the final result is prime, the pattern may be correct.
tricks.example: Results like 11 or 13 indicate a possible prime-based logic.

tricks.title: Category Depth Check
tricks.explanation: In word questions, check whether the words belong to a specific subcategory.

tricks.title: Alphabet Position Rule
tricks.explanation: In alphanumeric questions, convert letters into numbers.

tricks.title: Difference Square Logic
tricks.explanation: The difference between two letters may form a square number.

tricks.title: Reverse Pattern Check
tricks.explanation: Sometimes the pattern may follow reverse alphabetical order.

tricks.title: Fact Knowledge Advantage
tricks.explanation: Knowledge of history, science, and constitution helps in word classification.
tricks.example: Habeas Corpus and Mandamus are both writs.

tricks.title: Multi-Step Confirmation
tricks.explanation: Verify the pattern on at least three options before confirming.
tricks.example: If three options follow the rule and one does not, that one is the odd option.
